operator_request: let's record it in conjecture net and test it
governing_conjecture: A generic packet has a marked within-cycle crossing and an inter-cycle handoff. The proposed proton/neutron patterns return to the same sector kind next cycle, while the electron pattern may occupy a two-cycle orbit under a minimal reversible completion.

notation.M: Abstract main-sector label, encoded0 in the finite test.
notation.C: Abstract operator C-sector/codomain label, encoded1; not every linear-map codomain and not an established physical codimension assignment.
notation.index: A distinct cycle copy, not an exponent, dimension, tensor power, physical time or rotation angle.

minimal_completion_assumptions: One shared deterministic within-cycle map on two sectors
A context/mode retained across cycles, not erased at handoff
The minimum number of contexts needed to fit the three observations
Each fixed-context two-sector handoff is bijective, with no unretained environment; global reversibility of a larger system alone is not this assumption

predictions.common_crossing: The three observations fix the shared intra-cycle map to sector exchange.
predictions.memory_requirement: No context-free deterministic handoff fits neutron and electron, which share intermediate C but have different next sectors. At least two contexts are required.
predictions.completions: Anchor neutron context0 and electron context1. Enumerate all32 pairs of two-sector handoff functions and proton-context choices. Four fit the observed paths; exactly one has both handoffs bijective. It assigns proton/neutron context0 with flip handoff and electron context1 with identity handoff.
predictions.minimal_reversible_recurrence: For sector s and mode b, complete-cycle F(s,b)=(s XOR b,b): two fixed points and one two-cycle. The electron's C-entry phase is not automatically a new species.
predictions.underdetermination: Without the fixed-minimal-state bijectivity assumption, a constant-C handoff fits electron but loads and retains C instead of returning to M after two cycles.
predictions.environment_control: A globally reversible circuit with fresh initialized memory can implement constant-C coarse handoff. Global reversibility alone does not force the proposed two-sector period.
predictions.phase_control: The same electron sector exchange has exact unitary lifts X^2=I and J^2=-I. Sector period does not select amplitude sign, spin or physical time.
predictions.native_test: Current common-three-carrier L/G/N returns are nonzero projectors of ranks1/1/2; all three stages fix the active return image. Their untagged native return has period1, not an electron swap. A stage-independent raw-state sector reader cannot label the same active state differently at successive stages.
predictions.tagged_extension: An explicit two-sector register supplies compatible lifted maps on each actual native return image with its original induced metric and exact recovery. This is an added bookkeeping capability, not a source-derived M/C assignment or primitive physical process.

named_rivals: One sector-only handoff explains all three paths
Electron two-cycle return follows from the three paths alone
Reversibility of any enlarged system forces a bijective coarse handoff
A two-cycle sector orbit already supplies spinorial sign
Existing native return projectors already implement the electron sector swap
The explicit tag extension establishes physical sector/species identity
acceptance: Exhaust the finite completion classes, construct countermodels and the minimal reversible recurrence, and separately check actual native returns and an explicitly added tagged realization without promoting any physical assignment.
first_missing_physical_object: Independently grounded sector/context readers, stage and handoff operations and cycle marking on the actual source. Physical time/rotation and particle assignment require separate attachment.
